_note: B-45. MailFlowOps levers (PowerShell, offline mock mail-flow state in fixtures/mailflow; no Exchange Online is called). message.trace is R0 and quarantine.release R2 per the roadmap (W-SEC-03, W-M365-03, W-M365-04). Exchange cmdlet names are UNVERIFIED stand-ins; see fixtures/mailflow/SOURCES.md.

levers.name: message.trace
levers.description: List every person of the client who received one message, with delivery status and quarantine id; no subject or body. Mock of an Exchange Online message trace.

message_id.description: Internet message id of the reported message, angle brackets included

impact.L1: The person who reported a phish learns who else got it; nothing about anyone's mailbox changes.
impact.L2: The client sees how far one bad message reached, from its own mail flow only.
impact.L3: One scoped, audited read replaces a manual trace search, so the next recipient is warned sooner.
impact.L4: Another client's message id answers like an unknown one, so no office learns about another's mail.

levers.name: quarantine.release
levers.description: Release one quarantined message to one of its own recipients. Refused for high-confidence phish or malware. Mock of an Exchange Online quarantine release.

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the person the message was sent to and who asked for it

quarantine_id.description: Quarantine id of the held message, e.g. Q-1003

impact.L1: A person gets a wrongly held message; a wrong release puts a phish in their inbox, so a lead approves each one.
impact.L2: Legitimate client mail is not lost to quarantine, and phish or malware verdicts are never released by a lever.
impact.L3: Release requests become checked, approved and audited changes instead of portal clicks with no record.
impact.L4: A release goes only to the message's own recipients in the same client, never to anyone else.
